learning_outcomes.text: Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society, and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Possess learning skills that allow for lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply the knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.
Knowledge of the operation and application of electrical machines.
Techniques that allow for the acquisition of other learning outcomes, being aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering, including aspects of the latest advances.

Analyze complex products, processes and systems in their field of study; choose and apply relevant analytical, computational and experimental methods already established and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Practice with applicable techniques and methods to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects and conduct inquiry, analysis and synthesis, also considering their limitations, in their own area of specialization.
Apply the materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in their field of specialization.
Apply engineering practice standards in their specialization.
Acquire awareness and assume the social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial implications of engineering practice.
Recognize the need for continuous self-training and to undertake this activity throughout their professional life independently.

assessment_rules: The course is evaluated through a mandatory laboratory component (15% of the final grade) and either a progressive evaluation or a comprehensive final exam. The laboratory grade, comprising 55% from practice reports and 45% from a practical exam, requires a minimum of 4/10 in each part, and all practices must be completed to pass the course. For the progressive path, three block exams (30%, 30%, 25%) cover the course content, while the global path uses an 85% comprehensive final exam. To pass, a minimum score of 4/10 is required in all exam parts and laboratory components, with an overall final grade of 5/10 or higher; otherwise, the maximum grade is 4.5. Passed block exams are liberatory for the academic year, and students can retake exams to improve their grade.
